properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: REPSOL OIL & GAS USA LLC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 3/25/2026
Violation Code: 78a54 - GENERAL REQUIREMENTS - Operator failed to control and dispose of fluids, residual waste and drill cuttings, including tophole water, brines, drilling fluids, drilling muds, stimulation fluids, well servicing fluids, oil, and production fluids in a manner that prevents pollution of the waters of the Commonwealth and in accordance with 25 Pa. Code §§ 78a.55 – 78a.58 and 78a.60 – 78a.63.
Violation ID: 8268729
Permit API: 015-23994
Unconventional: Yes
County: Bradford
Municipality: Pike Township
Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 3/25/2026
Comments: On 03/24/2026 at 1132 hours Repsol reported (CTS#396090) that at 0600 hours they noticed fluid in the southside ditch of the Ugliuzza well pad that was going towards the catch basin. There was a hose that did not have a cap on it and the fluid was coming from the hose. They are estimating ~630 gallons (1 barrel=42 gallons) of produced water was released off containment. Resource Management was contracted to conduct remediation. At ~1525 hours Repsol contacted the DEP to update the amount release to be ~18,900 gallons. Four water trucks off-loading onsite each contained 4,620 gallons of produced fluid. It is estimated that the release traveled 1,143 feet downhill to the stream. A remediation plan is in place, and they are implementing it as we spoke. On 03/23/2026 at 2218 hours the first of five water trucks arrived onsite to off-load fluid for upcoming completion activities. From 2218-0319 hours 4 water trucks off-loaded onsite. At 0615 hours on 03/24/2026 a 5th water truck started offloading and immediately noticed the leak and stopped off-loading. On 03/25/2026 Repsol reported that as of 0700 hours ~10,500 gallons of fluid had been recovered from the stormwater channel and basin. On 03/25/2026 the DEP conducted an incident inspection report of Repsol's UGLIUZZA Well Pad. Water Quality Specialists Korey Starkey, Jonathan Pennings and I arrived at ~ 0930 hours. Licensed Professional Geologist Samuel Louderback arrived at approximately 1100 hours. The DEP met with Repsol representative Meagan DePue and Resource Management. Fenton Excavation was onsite excavating within the LOD to capture fluids during the inspection. Meagan stated that she contacted the PFBC and left a message. She informed us that a hose connected to the manifold was not connected to the produced fluid tanks and that it was hanging over the side of the secondary containment into the stormwater ditch while the first four trucks off-loaded (photo #2-6). The produced fluid then flowed to the stormwater basin (photo #7) and through the drainage pipe of the stormwater basin (photo #9) into a natural conveyance channel which reached a UNT to Rockwell Creek. The DEP, Repsol and Resource Management walked the impacted area together. Resource Management set up monitoring points and split sampled during that time. The fluids in the stormwater ditch were field measured for Electrical Conductivity (EC) at ~7.85 mS/cm. There was a sump pump in the stormwater ditch (photo #5). A sample was collected from the stormwater basin at 1204 hours (photo #8). The EC of the sampled fluids were >19.99 mS/cm. Fluids were able to escape the basin through an outflow pipe. Two sumps were constructed inside and outside of the basin (photo #7 and 10). Fluids collected in the sumps were being actively recovered.The EC of the drainage area beyond the stormwater basin was ~1.8 mS/cm and the soil EC was ~4.8 mS/cm (photo #11). The drainage area forms a conveyance channel ~500ft down from the release location. The EC of the conveyance channel was ~5.4 mS/cm (photo #12). There was a spring adding water to the channel ~900ft downstream from the release location. It was located above grade (photo #13). The EC of the spring was ~100 us/cm. We traveled ~500ft downstream the conveyance channel and obtained EC readings between 2.6-2.7 mS/cm (photo #14 and 15).We traveled downstream ~435ft. The conveyance channel EC was between 5.8-8.0 mS/cm (photo #16 and 17). The DEP and Resource Management each collected a sample at 1053 hours from the UNT upstream of where the released fluids discharged into the stream (photo #18). The DEP and Resource Management each collected a sample at 1118 hours from the UNT downstream of where the released fluids discharged into the stream (photo #22).The EC of Rockwell Creek ~1.4 miles away was ~0.15 mS/cm.

No fluids were observed on the pad surface surrounding the dehydration units. No staining was observed on the pad surface. A very small amount of water is present in the containment beneath the right dehydration unit. No E&S issues noted. Violations noted and considered immediately corrected.

properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: CHESAPEAKE APPALACHIA LLC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 5/08/2023
Violation Code: CSL 402(b) - POTENTIAL POLLUTION - Conducting an activity regulated by a permit issued pursuant to Section 402 of The Clean Streams Law to prevent the potential of pollution to waters of the Commonwealth without a permit or contrary to a permit issued under that authority by the Department.
Violation ID: 994241
Permit API: 015-23792
Unconventional: Yes
County: Bradford
Municipality: Tuscarora Twp
Inspection Type: Drilling/Alteration
Inspection Date: 5/08/2023
Comments: On 5/8/2023, DEP representative John Rogers conducted a drilling/alteration inspection at the Chesapeake Mowry 2 well site. It was 55 degrees and partly cloudy when I arrived on location. When I arrive on site, I met Chesapeake's Colter Dabney in the frac van. Colter described current operations as follows: A Halliburton frac fleet was on site, fracking two newly drilled wells. The crew is zippering back and forth between the wells and has completed 17 total stages. They expect to be finished at the site on 5/11/2023 and will move to the Mowry well site with fracking expected to begin there on 5/14/2023The two existing wells have been shut for the duration of the drilling and completion process. Pressures on each well was reported as 5H casing 965 psi and 2H casing 742 psi.Colter accompanied me on the inspection. I viewed a 10' x 20' water puddle northeast of the frac van that field tested at 1.477 mS conductance. Brine trucks were unloading to brine tanks in the northeast corner of the site. I screened some of the mud in this unloading area with a Hannah Groline soil probe with results at 0.4 mS conductance or less. Colter showed me three horsepowers that he said are diesel powered. These three trucks were only used for pump down. There are eight horsepowers that runoff electric power, being used for the fracking operations. The generators powering the frac fleet use natural gas produced from the area. The wireline truck is also electrical powered.I witnessed a 3' x 4' water puddle east of the freshwater AST that did field test at 2.13 mS conductance. I field tested water in the chemical additive area with results as high as 5.56 mS conductance. The chemical additive area is stationed in secondary containment. I discussed the various water puddles of elevated conductance with Colter. He said that he would have each of these puddles vacuumed up and would get a second vac truck on site to help. I discussed the high conductance water in the chemical additive area and the possibility of contamination to the pad surface if the containment liner was damaged. Most of the site appeared stable and well vegetated, meeting the 70% uniform, perennial, vegetative cover. PCSM is addressed on site by two retentive grading/infiltration areas. They are adequately stabilized and functioning as designed.Violations are still outstanding for inspection ID 3455915 for elevated conductance fluid detected on the unprotected pad surface during drilling operations.The DEP recommends the following:1. Use good housekeeping practices when handling chemicals at the site. Remove spilt product as soon as it is discovered.2. Determine the cause of elevated conductance discovered in the various water puddles around the site and clean up these areas.3. Use good housekeeping measures when removing the equipment and secondary containment from the site to prevent releasing pollution to the waters of the Commonwealth.I left the site at 1240 hours.

Inspection Date: 5/14/2026
Comments: This inspection was conducted to evaluate the status of violations issued on 9/18/2025 and 4/17/2026 associated with the construction of the well site for this proposed conventional well and the access road leading to it. Since the 4/17/2026 inspection, Trinity Mineral Partners (TMP) submitted multiple versions of an updated E and S plan that included additional BMPs and methods to stabilize all disturbed areas. At the time of this inspection, the latest version of the updated E and S plan has not yet met the expectations of the Department's Technical Services staff, as was indicated in a 5/11/2026 email to William Cenk.Throughout this inspection, we observed that a majority of the practices prescribed in the latest version of the updated E and S plan have been implemented. Inlet/outlet rock protection was placed at the installed culverts, rock filters placed in the roadside ditch in the vicinity of the well site for proposed Well # 3, and a combination of erosion blankets and mulch was applied to temporarily stabilize most of the disturbed areas. TMP indicated that seed was applied prior to mulching/placement of the erosion blanket. Erosion blanket was missing upslope of Culvert 1 and there was no evidence of hydro-seeding. The placement of grubbing material along the southern side of the access road that has displaced stream flow continues to result in accelerated erosion and washout along the southern edge of the road and perimeter of the well site for proposed Well # 4.The Department suggests the removal of the stockpile material from approximately the outlet location of Culvert 3 westerly to the newly established point of concentrated flow. Currently, it appears the streamflow is obstructed and migrated towards the pad/access road creating concentrated flow which cannot be stabilized. Without proper stabilization, the additional flow due to the construction activity appears to be causing accelerated erosion and sedimentation to Wetland G. The removal of the waste areas would potentially allow the flow to migrate back to its original drainage path and allow for successful installation of temporary stabilization BMPs, per plan. Department staff can be available for consultation/direction during the removal operation. Waste areas are not to be discarded in other floodways or wetlands. After the submission of the updated and complete E and S plan to Brian Ayers (brayers@pa.gov), temporary stabilization shall be finished. A follow up inspection will be conducted following the completion of the temporary stabilization. A preapplication meeting must be submitted/scheduled before June 15, 2026 in order to address any outstanding violations.Violations that were cited in the 9/18/2025 and 4/17/2026 inspection reports remain unaddressed.The following were in attendance for this inspection:DEP - Aquatic Biologist Samantha Lutz, Aquatic Biologist Jessica McDuff and WQSS Brian Ayers.Trinity Mineral Partners - Kyle Miller, Brian Bennett and Todd Fantaskey (Northwest Soil Services)

Report Details

Violation Code: CSL 402(b) - POTENTIAL POLLUTION - Conducting an activity regulated by a permit issued pursuant to Section 402 of The Clean Streams Law to prevent the potential of pollution to waters of the Commonwealth without a permit or contrary to a permit issued under that authority by the Department.
Violation ID: 8223738
Permit API: 117-20472
Unconventional: Yes
County: Tioga
Municipality: Delmar Township
Inspection Type: Routine/Complete Inspection
Inspection Date: 3/05/2025
Comments: On 3/5/2025, DEP representative John Rogers conducted a routine site inspection at Seneca's Butler 127 well site in Delmar Twp, Tioga Co. It was 47 degrees, overcast and raining when I arrived on location. Snow and water covered most of the pad surface. As I started the inspection, I witnessed a multicolored sheen on liquids near the wellheads. There were six wells staged for production and one plugged well monument. All wells were tagged with API/well permit numbers. No bubbling within the cellars was observed. I scanned the area around the wellheads to try and determine the possible source or extent of the multicolored sheen. I witnessed the multicolored sheen on the ground and on liquids on the south, east and north sides of the Butler 127 6H well. I did witness the multicolored sheen on the gravel pad surface north of the row of active wells and also extending into the vegetated areas. I discovered a V-shaped trench starting near the north side of the Butler 127 4H well; the trench measuring approximately 2-3' wide by 4" deep and extended 150'directly north, breaching through the perimeter berm. Milky colored liquid with the multicolored sheen was flowing along the trench and discharging past the perimeter berm, flowing down the fill slope and past a row of trees at the property line.I studied the snow/ice/water covered ground near the production tank and near the GPUs but did not witness a sheen in these areas. The production tank had secondary containment.Most of the site appeared stable and well vegetated, meeting the 70% uniform, perennial, vegetative cover. PCSM structures have not been installed at this site. Most of the pad surface has been vegetated with at least 70% uniform perennial vegetation but remains at well pad topography. I did witness an erosional channel starting at the well heads and crossing the vegetated area on the north side of the pad; erosion continuing through the breached perimeter berm and down the fill slope.I contacted Seneca's Dennis Wingrove to report the multicolored sheen. I left the location to gather necessary sampling supplies and met Seneca's Mike Olsyn when I returned. I showed Mike the extent of what I witnessed. I collected sample 9551-165 from flowing liquid within the erosion channel near the perimeter berm where a multicolored sheen was present; the sample to be analyzed for oil, grease and total petroleum hydrocarbons (TPH). Presence of a multicolored sheen indicates the potential of a release of a pollution causing substance. The release of an unknown volume of a pollution causing substance to the unprotected pad surface is a violation of CSL 402(b).Additional violations may be cited based on the sample results.Because of the large volume of fluids with the multicolored sheen discovered on the pad surface and flowing down and beyond the fill slope, the DEP recommends pursuing Act 2.The DEP recommends the following:1. Identify the cause of the multicolored sheen. Repair equipment or take steps to prevent a reoccurrence.2. Assess the area witnessed with the multicolored sheen on the south, east and north sides of the wells; on the north side of the pad; on the fill slope and continuing past the property line. Clean/report as necessary.3. Assess the condition of the north side of the pad, the north perimeter berm and the north fill slope for signs of erosion and repair as necessary.I left the site at 1600 hours.

Comments: On-site incident inspection in response to a release reported to the Department under inspection record 2867520. Inspection conducted with Environmental Trainee Eric Norman. Accompanied by Operator representatives Scott Cleveland, Laura Karosic, and Kyle Shirey. At the time of this inspection, drilling operations are actively ongoing for well 3M. Wells 1M and 5M have been drilled to the KOP. Mr. Cleveland showed the Department where the release originated as a result of a pipe disconnecting near the rig, where the released fluids hit the sound wall, and where a mist of this fluid was carried over the wall. A release of 5 bbl water, drill cuttings, and soap (Mega Mist HD) is estimated to have occurred. At this time, the vegetative matting on the western berm of the well pad outside of the sound wall has been replaced (Photos #1 and #2); the removed contaminated matting is currently wrapped in tarp at the base of this berm (Photo #1). There is rock on the edge of the pad, with a drain system underneath, between this berm and the sound wall (Photo #2). Mr. Cleveland reports only a very small amount of the released fluids got on this rock and the drains are currently closed; the drains will be checked for any released fluids prior to opening should any fluids have traveled within. Mr. Cleveland showed the Department the inside of the sound wall that was sprayed and the secondary containment that caught fluids (Photo #3). Between this secondary containment and sound wall is a thin strip of well pad (Photo #4). The sound wall and secondary containment, including the contents on the containment, were power-washed after the release. The operator hired a third party to remediate the release in accordance with Act 2 standards and this consultant is anticipated to be on-site tomorrow to begin this process. Violations are being issued for this reportable release of fluids.

Wells 1M and 5M have been drilled to the KOP. Mr. Cleveland showed the Department where the release originated as a result of a pipe disconnecting near the rig, where the released fluids hit the sound wall, and where a mist of this fluid was carried over the wall. A release of 5 bbl water, drill cuttings, and soap (Mega Mist HD) is estimated to have occurred. At this time, the vegetative matting on the western berm of the well pad outside of the sound wall has been replaced (Photos #1 and #2); the removed contaminated matting is currently wrapped in tarp at the base of this berm (Photo #1). Comments: On March 21, 2025, the Department conducted a follow up Inspection of the RWS Development 001 Well in response to an incident which is documented in IR 3941481 and 3941519 where violations were issued for a brine release.At the time of the inspection the well site appeared unchanged from the Department's previous inspection on 3/20/2025.At the time of this inspection, the Department observed charred vegetation on a slope adjacent to the well site, no erosion or sedimentation issues were observed. A wellhead was observed with a well tag fixed to it with all required information posted on it, and no active fluid leaks or fluid discharges were observed coming from or near this wellhead. Other production equipment was observed on site and appeared to be charred, no active fluid leaks or fluid discharges were observed coming from or near any of this production equipment. A production tank was observed on site with a large hole in its side, the tank had approximately 1-2 in of fluid pooled at the bottom of it, no active fluid leaks or fluid discharges were observed coming from or near this production tank.A soil conductivity reading was taken directly under the hole in the tank with a reading of 10.16mS. The Department observed standing fluid in the ditch/channel in several locations. The Department observed 2 booms installed in the ditch. Conductivity readings were taken of the fluid in the ditch in several locations with readings of 10.43mS, 7.28mS, 1.27mS, 0.93mS, 0.68mS, 0.78mS. The conductivity readings appeared to decrease with distance from the well/production tank. No standing fluid was observed in the ditch in approximately the last 45 feet prior to terminating near the stream. There did not appear to be a recent flow path of fluid in the section of ditch from the last location of standing water to the remainder of ditch before the stream. Conductivity readings were taken in this area of the ditch with readings of 0.53mS, 0.38mS, and 0.46mS.A conductivity reading was taken upstream of where the ditch appears to terminate with a reading of 0.67mS. A conductivity reading was then taken in the stream in the area where the ditch appears to terminate prior to the stream with a reading of 0.76mS. No sheen, discoloration, or foaming was observed in the stream.Based on the Department's observations and conductivity readings obtained, it appears that the conductivity readings are comparable to the previous inspections in regards to distance and levels of elevated readings in the ditch. It appears that released fluids may have been contained to the portions of the ditch where standing fluid was observed, and it did not appear from the observations and readings that there was a release into Waters of the Commonwealth.Prior to leaving the site, the Department called operator representative Ben Dickun to inquire when remediation was going to begin. Mr. Dickun stated they have contacted their consultant (Moody) and that work to remediate as well as a site assessment/sampling by Moody was scheduled to occur on Tuesday, 3/25/2025. The Department recommended during the call that immediate measures are properly implemented to commence remediation in response to the brine release that occurred onsite during the 3/19/2025 incident to prevent further migration of the onsite pollution and prevent pollution into WOC.Based on today's inspection, violations issued during IR 3941481 and 3941519 shall remain outstanding.

Comments: On December 9, 2025, the Department conducted a Complaint Inspection of Oil and Gas Management Inc's Neilan 1 well site located in Somerset Township, Somerset County.At the time of this inspection, the well site was snow covered, therefore, the vegetative cover of the well site, along with erosion and sedimentation issues throughout the well site and along the access road could not be assessed at the time of this inspection. At the time of this inspection, the Department observed a wellhead with a well tag fixed to it that had all required information posted on it. No active fluid leaks or fluid discharges were observed to be coming from or near the wellhead. A small production tank was observed to be connected to the wellhead and no fluid leaks or fluid discharges were observed to be coming from or near this production tank either.At the time of this inspection, the Department observed production equipment connected to a meter box, no active fluid leaks or fluid discharges were observed to be coming from or near this production equipment or meter box. Inside the Meter Box, the Department observed production paper that was dated 10/27/2023. A pile of pipes was observed on the ground adjacent to the meter box and production equipment, the Department recommends any equipment not in use be removed from the well site. At the time of this inspection, the Department observed two other production tanks on site that both appeared to be connected to the well. The tank on the left did not have any observable holes or corrosive parts, however, the tank on the right had several corroded pipes at the base of the tank and a pipe that was completely broken in half due to corrosion at the top of the tank. No active fluid leaks or fluid discharges were observed to be coming from or near either production tank at this time. A conductivity meter was utilized to screen the area around the right production tank as well as utilized to collect a background soil conductivity reading of 0.234 mS taken upslope and adjacent to the well site. A soil conductivity readings of 1.285 mS was collected below a corroded pipe, and then readings of 0.0089 mS and 0.0694 mS were collected downslope of this area. The reading taken below the corroded pipe is elevated when compared to background, subjugating that a release likely occurred here. The Department is requesting the Operator submit a written response within seven (7) days of the receipt of this report. This written response should include an incident report, a timeline of remedial measures, and plan for remediation of the spill or release.The Department is requesting how the Operator quantified the amount spilled. The Department also requests the waste manifest from the site remediation be submitted upon receipt. Based on today's inspection, violations are being issued for the broken corroded pipe near the top of the production tank and for a release from corroded piping on the production tank.

Report Details

Permit API: 123-44951
Unconventional: No
County: Warren
Municipality: Pleasant Township
Inspection Type: Complaint Inspection

Comments: This well was inspected as part of an on going stray gas migration case involving gas migrating into a private water supply (CTS#373559). The well head and casing strings were observed at the time of inspection for leaks, deterioration, and possible failures. As part of the investigation 3 slam bar holes were placed into the ground approximately 1-2 feet from the well head to identify if any methane was migrating from the well-bore. All valves were open and the well is currently equipped for production. 2 check valves were in place on the production lines and were oriented correctly. Well records, production reports, and mechanical integrity assessment reports were reviewed to assist in the investigation. 3% Methane was detected in slam bar hole #3 utilizing a MSA ALTAIR 5X Meter which was calibrated on 07/17/2023, a viable methane sample was not attainable at the time of inspection. At this time the following violations are being issued against this well. VIOLATION: 78.86 - CASING AND CEMENTING – DEFECTIVE CASING OR CEMENTING - Operator failed to report defect in a well that has defective, insufficient or improperly cemented casing to the Department within 24 hours of discovery. Operator failed to correct defect or failed to submit a plan to correct the defect for approval by the Department within 30 days. VIOLATION:78.73(a) - GENERAL PROVISION FOR WELL CONSTRUCTION AND OPERATION - Operator failed to construct and operate the well in accordance with 25 Pa. Code Chapter 78 and ensure that the integrity of the well is maintained and health, safety, environment and property are protected. VIOLATION:78.88(d) - OPERATING WELLS – MECHANICAL INTEGRITY OF OPERATING WELLS - Operator failed to immediately notify the Department and take corrective actions to repair or replace defective equipment or casing for wells exhibiting progressive corrosion, rusting or other signs of equipment deterioration that compromise the integrity of the well. VIOLATION: 78.81(a)1 - CASING AND CEMENTING – GENERAL PROVISIONS - Operator conducted casing and cementing activities that failed to allow for effective control of the well at all times At this time the department is requesting an investigation into the possible source of methane to be conducted by the operator.

Comments: Site inspection conducted to review drill cuttings processing activity and secondary containment conditions at the Taft 851 well pad. The 206HU will be drilled top to total depth with the rig batch drilling the surface and intermediate sections for the remaining seven wells. There are five wells in production and currently flowing to sales at this pad. Fluid control in the rig backyard is being handled by Paragon Integrated Services. The rig is drilling the intermediate string on water based mud (WBM) with polymer flocculants and calcium nitrate in use to assist removal of solids from the drilling fluid. Drill cuttings are removed from the system using two sets of shakers and two centrifuges. Fluid removed from the centrifuges is returned to a catch tank and pumped back to the mud tanks for recirculation downhole (photos 3-5). Solids control in the backyard is being conducted by White's Energy Services. Drill cuttings and excess liquid are solidified using wood crumble material and are stored in steel bins awaiting haulage to the landfill. Seneca submitted a Request for Approval of Alternate Waste Management Practices (OG-71) Form A application for the Taft Pad on 4/25/25. The Department approved the request on 5/1/25. The request for the approval of Alternative Waste Management Practices is for drill cuttings processing and solids removal from drilling mud. See photos and comments in the on-site processing findings section of this inspection report below, and refer to the Taft OG-71 Form A application, eFACTS Authorization ID#1525611.Site inspection followed several days of heavy precipitation. A vacuum truck is pumping precipitation water out of secondary containment structures for the frac tank battery at the west side of the pad. The Department observed yellow floc water tanks labeled as cement water near the north side of the rig. The Department recommends that floc water tanks and freshwater tanks near the barite silos be labeled for contents. During this inspection, fluid with elevated conductivity (4.74 mS/cm) is observed in the ditch line between the pad rock and the berm along the north side of the well pad (photo 13). This water was traced and found to be entering Sediment Basin 1 along the rock lined channel sloping down from the pad surface. Additionally, water was observed draining from the sed basin, entering the level spreader, and exiting to a brushy wooded area north of the LOD with a conductivity reading of 2.16 mS/cm. The Department recommends containing and collecting water which exceeds the Department 78a.60b(3) discharge limitation of 1,000 uS/cm or 1 mS/cm. Violations remain outstanding against permit #117-22231 for pollutional water found on site and documented in Inspection Reports #3736567 and #3724668.

properties.summary: Environmental Health & Safety violation issued on 6/17/2026 to MCCOOL JOHN E in Cherry Grove Township, Warren county. 78.57(a) - CONTROL, STORAGE AND DISPOSAL OF PRODUCTION FLUIDS - Operator failed to collect the brine and other fluids produced during operation, service and plugging of the well in a tank, pit or a series of pits or tanks, or other device approved by the Department or Operator discharged brine or other fluids on or into the ground or into waters of the Commonwealth.
properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: MCCOOL JOHN E
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 6/17/2026
Violation Code: 78.57(a) - CONTROL, STORAGE AND DISPOSAL OF PRODUCTION FLUIDS - Operator failed to collect the brine and other fluids produced during operation, service and plugging of the well in a tank, pit or a series of pits or tanks, or other device approved by the Department or Operator discharged brine or other fluids on or into the ground or into waters of the Commonwealth.
Violation ID: 8278641
Permit API: 123-47075
Unconventional: No
County: Warren
Municipality: Cherry Grove Township
Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 6/17/2026
Comments: This inspection is being conducted in response to the observation of production fluid exiting the secondary containment of the Lot 740 tank battery. Conventional well Lot 740 15 (API # 123-47075) is nearest the tank battery. The conventional well appears to be plumbed for production. An old sign displaying the API number, well name, and the wrong operator contact information is posted on a tree near the location. The sign should be updated with the current operator's name and contact information. The tank battery at the site has 2 steel tanks and a separator situated within an earthen secondary containment. The secondary containment was approximately 60ft x 20ft. Evidence of staining, dead vegetation, numerous deer tracks, and conductivity readings over range (greater than 20,000 mS/cm maximum that field meter can measure) were present in standing water throughout the entire secondary containment. This would indicate a large volume of production fluid filled the entire containment at one time (see photo 1). At the time of the inspection, the ground within the secondary containment was saturated with production fluid with some ponding throughout. A small amount of crude oil was also identified within the escaped production fluid. A containment drain inlet was located at a low point in the front left corner within the containment. A conductivity reading of 17.17 mS/cm was measured at the drain inlet (see photo 2). The ponding production fluid was flowing into the drain's inlet, exiting the containment through the drain outlet located at the exterior front left corner of the secondary containment (see photo 3). The containment drain was open and unattended at the time of this inspection. Sample 001 was collected at 13:10 at the containment drain outlet for further testing. A conductivity reading was also taken at this location measuring over range (see photo 4). The production fluid flowed from the containment drain into the road ditch traveling south approximately 50 feet (see photo 5). The escaped production fluid also flowed north in the road ditch approximately 10 feet before entering a road culvert where it continued westward into the woods for approximately 150 feet (see photo 6). The vegetation in the path of flow was dead, the ground was muddy and imprinted with deer tracks, and the conductivity readings measured high throughout the entire length of travel. The conductivity was measured near the apparent end of impact with a reading of 8.51 mS/cm in a puddle.The containment drain is required to be closed when unattended and the regulations state that any discharge is to only consist of precipitation that accumulates inside the containment, not production fluids. On June 18, 2026 a phone call was made to the operator, John McCool, in which he stated his intentions to work towards achieving compliance. He explained that the fluids currently stored in the tanks will be pumped empty and examined for leaks. If any leaks are identified, the tanks will be repaired or replaced. An excavator will be used to remove the contaminated soil within the secondary containment and beyond the containment drain exit following the path of travel through the woods. Upon disposing of the contaminated soils at an approved facility, a copy of the disposal slip from the landfill is expected to be provided to the Department. Confirmatory sampling will be required to confirm the impacts from the release have been sufficiently remediated. The Department's Policy 800-5000-001- "Addressing Spills and Releases at Oil and Gas Well Sites and Access Roads" sets forth the procedure to be followed to resolve the violations associated with the spill/discharge/release documented in this Notice of Violation ("NOV"), by using either the Act 2 or the Alternative Remediation Process. Follow up inspections will be performed routinely until the cleanup is deemed complete.

Various buckets and drums with a petroleum substance are located around the site (photos #7-9). Petroleum substances are pooled and stained around the ground specifically near the drum in photo #7. Representatives from Minard Run Oil Co. were contacted regarding the oil on the ground and sent personnel the following morning (05/08/2024) and estimated that approximately 3 gallons of oil was released. They brought equipment and excavated the affected area and removed the drums of oil so that there were no visual or odor traces of the release (photo #10).No standing water was observed onsite.Areas surrounding the site are wooded appears to be stabilized. There was no evidence of accelerated erosion or sedimentation.The DEP recommends backfilling and re-stabilizing the affected area upon completion of clean up.Based on the results of this inspection, a violation of CSL402(b) is cited against API#: 105-21086 and noted as immediately corrected.I departed the site at 1400 hours.

properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: SENECA RESOURCES CO LLC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 3/09/2021
Violation Code: CSL 402(b) - POTENTIAL POLLUTION - Conducting an activity regulated by a permit issued pursuant to Section 402 of The Clean Streams Law to prevent the potential of pollution to waters of the Commonwealth without a permit or contrary to a permit issued under that authority by the Department.
Violation ID: 910053
Permit API: 117-20562
Unconventional: Yes
County: Tioga
Municipality: Middlebury Twp
Inspection Type: Routine/Complete Inspection
Inspection Date: 3/09/2021
Comments: The Department of Environmental Protection (DEP) conducted a ROUTINE inspection of the Seneca Resources - Gee 832 Well Site located in Middlebury Twp, Tioga Co. on 3/9/21 @0950 hours. The weather was 45 degrees and sunny. No activity or personnel was observed onsite. The site consists of a long access road, well pad and perimeter controls. The majority of the well pad was clear of snow and ice with some piles still melting along the edges. Frozen fluid was observed in the infiltration basin off the corner of the well pad. What appeared to be frost was observed on the production tank onsite. Upon closer inspection, the tank appeared to be covered in crystalized salt originating from the top hatch of the tank . The front 1/3 of the "Highland" production tank and a small ~5'x5' area in front of the tank were observed to have the salt material on it. The pad surface in front of the tank was observed damp. Soil conductivity of the damp area was measured with a Groline soil conductivity probe and found to be >4.0mS/cm directly adjacent to the yellow barrel. Other areas screened within the 5'x5' area in front of the tank were found to have a field measured conductivity of 2.18mS/cm and 1.7mS/cm. Due to the lack of cell phone service onsite, I traveled to a nearby well pad with known cell phone service to contact the operator. I then returned to the well site to complete the inspection. Seneca representative Jake Chambers arrived onsite in response to the release. Mr. Chambers and I discussed the possible causes for the release and the impacted area. Mr. Chambers stated he would immediately mobilize people and equipment to wash down the tank and remove any impacted pad material Jeff Passerrello, Seneca Resources, submitted confirmation of the remediation of the release at the Gee 832 Well Pad via email. Mr. Passerrello stated the release was estimated to have happened between Sunday 3/7/21 and the morning of the DEP inspection. The operator had unloaded the wells to the production tanks on Sunday, which they believe caused a mist of production fluid to coat the tank and gravel. The release was estimated to be approximately 5 gallons. Crews removed the impacted gravel, which was placed into 3 drums. A depth of 3" of material was removed from in front of the tank. The tank was also cleaned with freshwater and scrub brushes. Violations of the following regulations are cited as Immediately Corrected: 25 Pa Code 78a57(a)Control, Storage and disposal of production fluids CSL402(b)Potential Pollution SWMA 301 Management of residual waste I departed the site at 1145 hours.

properties.summary: Environmental Health & Safety violation issued on 3/01/2024 to EQT ARO LLC in Plunketts Creek Township, Lycoming county. 78a56(a) - TEMPORARY STORAGE - Operator failed to contain regulated substances and wastes used at or generated at a well site in a tank, series of tanks or other storage structures approved by the Department.
properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: EQT ARO LLC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 3/01/2024
Violation Code: 78a56(a) - TEMPORARY STORAGE - Operator failed to contain regulated substances and wastes used at or generated at a well site in a tank, series of tanks or other storage structures approved by the Department.
Violation ID: 8177800
Permit API: 081-21938
Unconventional: Yes
County: Lycoming
Municipality: Plunketts Creek Township
Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 3/01/2024
Comments: Arrived onsite in response to a reported release of 10 barrels of produced water. It was reported that there were 2 barrels off of containment and 8 barrels on containment. The release occurred from a low pressure line on a fracking pump while the line was being flushed with fresh water from an AST onsite. The mixture of fresh and produced water sprayed out as a mist over the secondary containment and the pad. The release was reported around 23:00 on 2/29/24.The affected area was about 60' southeast of the wells near the center of the pad. Tobias Welding and Machining began scraping the impacted area on 2/29/24. On 3/1/24, Penn E and R arrived and continued to scrape the area based on visual and conductivity screening. The scraped area was about 77' by 26' around and 2" to 4" deep. Penn E and R was in the process of setting up confirmation sampling for Act 2 remediation.DEP screened for conductivity inside and surrounding the scraped area. Puddles within the scraped area ranged from 0.84 to 0.96 millisiemens per centimeter (mS/cm) and the soil was below 0.10 mS/cm. Puddles surrounding the scraped area were 0.34 to 0.65 mS/cm. Soil conductivity readings were attempted outside the impacted area but the pad was too compacted.The removed material was being hauled to the neighboring Bieber Sisters Pad A where it was stored in a covered rolloff container on secondary containment. The material will remain on the pad until characterization samples are completed and it can be properly disposed of. Photo 3 shows the rolloff with about half of the removed material. The rest of the material was being hauled to the rolloff while DEP was leaving the site.Based on a conversation with Zac Subra, EQT, the initial reported volume of the release may have been overestimated. However, since an exact volume was not know EQT will still follow the remediation requirements of Act 2.It is recommended that the pad be screened when secondary containment is pulled to be certain that no produced water seeped under the containment as a result of the release.The result of this inspection is Violations Noted for CSL 402(b), 78a56(a), and SWMA 301.
